A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerLDiff research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original NuScenes and KITTI generation experiments, downstream perception results, component ablations, and qualitative studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation and perception results and adds experiments involving MagicDrive mask integration, a ControlNet-based variant, and additional qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The principal PerLDiff pipeline remains unchanged. Appendix C.4 adds an adaptation inserting object masks into MagicDrive's bounding-box token attention, and C.5 introduces a ControlNet-based experimental variant. These are procedural adaptations; the revised latent-variable notation in the original pipeline merely clarifies its existing sequential updates.

E1.justification: NuScenes, KITTI, their perception tasks, and the NuScenes-to-KITTI transfer setting remain. Qualitative scenario coverage changes: v3 explicitly tests alignment across continuous frames in Figure 13, while v1's dedicated object-size and forward-position manipulation sweeps in Figures 8-9 are no longer reported.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds reproduced MagicDrive* comparisons using both BEVFusion and BEVFormer, retaining the published MagicDrive and existing BEVControl/BEVGen entries. MagicDrive also joins Figure 1's qualitative comparison, and Table 9 introduces an evaluated ControlNet-based comparator. This extends the existing comparison framework.

E3.justification: Table 5 extends the masking-weight settings from 1, 3, and 5 to include 10. Table 8 includes mAVE in the new mask-integration experiment, and Appendix C.5 introduces a backbone-replacement control. Existing splits, resolutions, training budget, and sampling settings remain; no evaluation-protocol change is documented to explain the revised FID values.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens analysis through mask transfer into MagicDrive (C.4, Table 8), a ControlNet-versus-GLIGEN architecture study with training curves (C.5, Table 9, Figure 9), and extended masking-weight sensitivity. Figures 13 and 15 add temporal-alignment and background-error cases. These address portability, architectural choice, and failure behavior beyond v1's component, CFG, and view-attention analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's training-loss plots do not specify uncertainty estimates across repeated runs. Revised averages in the CFG discussion retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: FID values change substantially across Tables 1 and 4-7: PerLDiff changes from 25.06 to 13.36 in Table 1 and from 26.61 to 15.67 in Table 6, reversing its ranking against retained MagicDrive scores. These are unexplained numerical revisions, not established same-setting performance gains. Tables 8-9 and the extended Table 5 add results, while existing detection, segmentation, KITTI, and downstream augmentation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion preliminaries and attention mathematics are retained. Distinct intermediate variables in Equations 5-6, Equation 10, and Algorithm 1 make existing sequential updates explicit without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about geometric masking, precise controllability, NuScenes/KITTI performance, and synthetic-data utility. The supplementary experiments do not redefine the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v1 defends its worse FID by prioritizing control and avoiding redundant imagery; v3 replaces this argument with claimed superiority over MagicDrive and attributes residual background mismatch to masking constraints (Section 4.2, Appendix D). v3 also adds a projected-size/depth explanation for KITTI results, qualifies benefits of increasing masking weights, discusses architectural limits of MagicDrive integration, and argues that appearance details are less important than position/category consistency for temporal detection.

D1.justification: v3 newly reports two days of training in Appendix B, identifies BEVFusion as camera-only, and explains attention-map visualization through object-wise averaging at DDIM step 50 in the final UNet block. These clarify existing experiments; the main hyperparameters, hardware, and code/model availability statement are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and main related-work discussion remain essentially unchanged. Appendices C.4-C.5 add substantive positioning against MagicDrive's unified attention representation and ControlNet's architecture, explaining claimed advantages and constraints relative to these existing approaches.

P1.justification: Most introductory, related-work, method, and concluding prose is retained. Changes standardize PerLDiff terminology, replace many references to BEV annotations with 3D annotations, rewrite portions of the results discussion and Appendix D, number related-work subsections, and move Algorithm 1 into Appendix C.3.

P2.justification: v3 adopts an ICLR-style layout and substantially revises the visual presentation. Figure 1 is replaced, Tables 1 and 5 gain rows, Tables 8-9 and an attention schematic and training curves are added, and the appendix galleries are reorganized around new comparisons, temporal alignment, and background errors. Several existing displays are retained under new numbering rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: The new MagicDrive mask and ControlNet ablations address portability and architectural-choice questions absent from v1, while implementation details and background-failure discussion improve transparency. These provide a limited net benefit despite removal of dedicated size/position demonstrations. The unexplained large FID revisions limit confidence in the strengthened image-fidelity comparison and do not themselves establish improved paper quality.
